questions.stem: About renal work, the correct propositions are:
options: ΔW = n₀RT·ln(ωu/ωpl) is the work needed to transfer n₀ osmoles of a substance from the blood to the urine
ωu and ωpl are the molar masses of the solute in the urine and in the plasma
Renal work is the energy expended by the kidneys to filter the blood and to secrete or reabsorb solutes such as sodium, urea or glucose
When ωu = ωpl, the renal work is maximal
For a fixed n₀ and plasma osmolarity, a higher urinary osmolarity of the solute increases the renal work
questions.explanation: ΔW = n₀RT·ln(ωu/ωpl), where ωu and ωpl are the solute's osmolarities (not molar masses) in urine and plasma. If ωu = ωpl, ln(1) = 0, so the work is zero, not maximal.

questions.stem: A patient eliminates 0.48 mol of urea per 24 h in 1.2 L of urine. His uremia (mass concentration of urea in the blood) is 0.3 g/L (M urea = 60 g/mol). The ratio ωu/ωpl of urea equals:
questions.explanation: ωu = n₀/V = 0.48/1.2 = 0.4 osmol/L; ωpl = Cp/M = 0.3/60 = 0.005 osmol/L, so the ratio is 80. 1.33 comes from dividing by the mass concentration (0.3 g/L) without converting it to osmol/L.

questions.stem: (Continued: 0.48 mol of urea per 24 h, ωu/ωpl = 80, T = 310 K, R = 8.31 SI.) The minimum power provided by each kidney to eliminate this urea is:
questions.explanation: ΔW = 0.48 × 8.31 × 310 × ln(80) ≈ 5418 J per day; per kidney P = ½ ΔW/Δt = 5418/172800 ≈ 31.4 mW. 62.7 mW is the power of both kidneys together; 13.6 mW uses log₁₀ instead of ln; 30.3 mW uses T = 300 K.

questions.stem: Two subjects eliminate the same number of osmoles of urea per day, with the same plasma urea osmolarity ωpl = 0.005 osmol/L and the same temperature. The urinary osmolarity of urea is 0.3 osmol/L for subject 1 and 0.6 osmol/L for subject 2:
options: The kidneys of subject 2 provide more work
The renal work of subject 2 is twice that of subject 1
W₂/W₁ ≈ 1.17
Subject 2 has the larger urine volume
The renal work does not depend on the temperature
questions.explanation: W ∝ ln(ωu/ωpl): W₂/W₁ = ln(120)/ln(60) ≈ 1.17, not 2, because the work depends on the logarithm of the osmolarity ratio. Same n₀ with a higher ωu means a smaller urine volume (V = n₀/ωu), so subject 2 has the smaller volume; T appears directly in ΔW = n₀RT·ln(ωu/ωpl).

questions.stem: A patient with renal insufficiency is asked to drink plenty of water; the amount of urea to eliminate and the uremia remain unchanged. The correct propositions are:
options: The urine volume increases
The urinary osmolarity of urea increases
The ratio ωu/ωpl decreases
The power provided by each kidney decreases
The renal work increases because more water has to be filtered
questions.explanation: Drinking water increases urine volume and decreases the urinary osmolarity of urea (ωu = n₀/V), so ln(ωu/ωpl) and the work imposed on the nephrons fall (e.g. 21.97 mW → 16.08 mW in the course exercise). This protects the remaining nephrons; water intake does not increase renal work.

questions.stem: About transport phenomena, the correct propositions are:
options: They are exchanges of water and solutes across membranes between the intracellular and extracellular compartments
They depend on the nature of the transported particles (size, charge, shape)
They depend on the osmolarity of the solutions
They are independent of the pressures exerted on either side of the membrane
There are only two types of transport: passive and active
questions.explanation: Transport phenomena depend on the nature of the particles, the osmolarity of the solutions and the pressures on either side of the membrane. There are three types: passive, facilitated passive and active.

questions.stem: Passive transport occurs via thermal agitation of particles. The correct propositions are:
options: A difference in concentrations causes diffusion
A difference in pressures causes migration
A difference in electrical potentials causes convection
A difference in pressures causes convection
Passive transport consumes chemical energy from ATP hydrolysis
questions.explanation: Concentration difference → diffusion; pressure difference → convection; electrical potential difference → migration. Only active transport consumes ATP.

options: Facilitated passive transport requires ATP hydrolysis
Active transport is carried out by membrane transporters and consumes chemical energy (ATP hydrolysis)
Facilitated passive transport moves certain particles through specific channels, by proteins, without energy expenditure
Active transport is driven only by the thermal agitation of particles
Facilitated passive transport is one of the three types of transport
questions.explanation: Facilitated passive transport uses membrane transporters (specific channels) without energy expenditure; active transport uses membrane transporters and consumes ATP. Thermal agitation drives simple passive transport.

questions.stem: The same solute is placed in compartments (1) and (2) of the setup shown, with C₁ᵢ > C₂ᵢ and V₁ = V₂. The correct propositions are:
options: The solute diffuses from (2) to (1)
Diffusion continues until C₁f = C₂f
At the final state, C∞ = (C₁ᵢ + C₂ᵢ)/2
The total number of moles of solute decreases during diffusion
By convention, liquid flows are assumed to occur before solute flows
questions.explanation: Solute diffuses from (1) to (2) (high to low concentration) until the concentrations are equal; the total number of moles is conserved, giving C∞ = (C₁ᵢ + C₂ᵢ)/2 when V₁ = V₂. By convention, solute flows occur first, then liquid flows.

questions.stem: A dialysis membrane separates compartment (1) (V₁ = 1 L, C₁ᵢ = 0.2 mol/L) and compartment (2) (V₂ = 3 L, C₂ᵢ = 0.04 mol/L) of the same solute. The final concentration C∞ is:
options: 0.12 mol/L
0.16 mol/L
0.32 mol/L
0.06 mol/L
0.08 mol/L
questions.explanation: C∞ = (C₁ᵢV₁ + C₂ᵢV₂)/(V₁ + V₂) = (0.2 + 0.12)/4 = 0.08 mol/L. 0.12 mol/L is the simple mean (C₁ᵢ + C₂ᵢ)/2, valid only if V₁ = V₂; 0.32 is the total number of moles.

questions.stem: About Fick's law Q = dn/dt = −DS′·dC/dx, the correct propositions are:
options: [Q] = mol/s
[D] = m²/s
[dC/dx] = mol/m³
S′ is the total surface area of the membrane
D is the diffusion coefficient of the solute
questions.explanation: Q is a molar flow rate (mol/s), D the solute's diffusion coefficient (m²/s) and dC/dx the concentration gradient in mol/m⁴ (mol/m³ per m). S′ is the permeable pore surface area, not the total membrane surface S.

questions.stem: Two compartments with C₁ᵢ > C₂ᵢ are separated by a membrane of width l, the x-axis going from (1) to (2) with its origin at the membrane. About the initial molar flow rate Qᵢ:
options: ΔCᵢ = C₂ᵢ − C₁ᵢ is negative
Qᵢ = −DS′·ΔCᵢ/l is positive: the solute flows along +x, from (1) to (2)
Qᵢ increases when the membrane is wider (larger l)
Qᵢ = (DS′/l)·|ΔCᵢ|
The minus sign in Fick's law means the solute moves up its concentration gradient
questions.explanation: With dCᵢ ≡ ΔCᵢ = C₂ᵢ − C₁ᵢ < 0 and dx ≡ l, Qᵢ = −DS′ΔCᵢ/l = (DS′/l)|ΔCᵢ| > 0. Qᵢ is inversely proportional to l, and the minus sign means the solute moves down its gradient (from high to low concentration).

questions.stem: A solute (D = 10⁻⁹ m²/s) diffuses through a membrane of width l = 10 µm and permeable pore area S′ = 2 cm². Initially C₁ᵢ = 50 mmol/L and C₂ᵢ = 10 mmol/L. The initial molar flow rate Qᵢ is:
options: 8 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol/s
8 × 10⁻⁷ mol/s
8 × 10⁻³ mol/s
4 × 10⁻⁷ mol/s
questions.explanation: Qᵢ = DS′|ΔCᵢ|/l = 10⁻⁹ × 2×10⁻⁴ × 40 / 10⁻⁵ = 8 × 10⁻⁷ mol/s (40 mmol/L = 40 mol/m³). 8 × 10⁻¹⁰ forgets to convert mmol/L to mol/m³; 8 × 10⁻³ leaves S′ in cm²; 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ uses the sum of concentrations instead of the difference.

questions.stem: About the mass flow rate and the diffusive flux of a solute, the correct propositions are:
options: Written with the mass concentration Cp, Fick's law gives the mass flow rate dm/dt, in kg/s
The diffusive flux Jd = Q/S is the molar flow rate per unit area, S being the membrane surface
[Jd] = mol·s⁻¹·m⁻²
Jd = −D·(S′/S)·dC/dx
A "rate" of X is X per unit surface, while a "flux" of X is X per unit time
questions.explanation: Q = dm/dt = −DS′·dCp/dx in kg/s; Jd = Q/S = −D(S′/S)·dC/dx in mol/s·m². The memo is inverted in E: rate of X = X/time, flux of X = X/surface.

questions.stem: (Continued: Qᵢ = 8 × 10⁻⁷ mol/s, S′ = 2 cm².) The total membrane surface is S = 10 cm². The initial diffusive flux Jd is:
options: 8 × 10⁻⁴ mol·s⁻¹·m⁻²
8 × 10⁻⁸ mol·s⁻¹·m⁻²
4 × 10⁻³ mol·s⁻¹·m⁻²
8 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol·s⁻¹·m⁻²
1.6 × 10⁻⁴ mol·s⁻¹·m⁻²
questions.explanation: Jd = Q/S = 8×10⁻⁷ / 10⁻³ m² = 8 × 10⁻⁴ mol·s⁻¹·m⁻². Dividing by S′ instead of S gives 4 × 10⁻³; leaving S in cm² gives 8 × 10⁻⁸; multiplying by S gives 8 × 10⁻¹⁰.
